title: Here, there, and everywhere!
goals: Say what is in a city and what is not. Use there is / there are with some, any, several, many and a lot of.
Name places and attractions in a city. Understand good and bad opinions in a travel blog.
Give and understand directions, orders and advice with the imperative, also in the negative (Don't forget…).
Show where a place is on a map: on the corner of, next to, between, across from.
Repeat directions to check them, and fix a mistake.
Describe a place with adjectives, give reasons (because, this way) and write a short paragraph that recommends it.

learn.title: There is / There are with some, any, several, many, a lot of
learn.html:
We use it to say that something exists in a place. In English you always need there. There is is for singular nouns; there are is for plural nouns. The verb agrees with the word that comes after.

AffirmativeNegativeQuestionShort answer
There is a museum. (There's)There isn't a museum.Is there a museum?Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.
There are some parks.There aren't any parks.Are there any parks?Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.
There are several festivals.There aren't many festivals.Are there many festivals?Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.
There are a lot of tourists.There aren't a lot of tourists.Are there a lot of tourists?Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.
QuantityWhere we use itExample
someaffirmative sentencesThere are some good shows.
severalaffirmative sentencesThere are several hotels.
a lot ofaffirmative, negative and questionsThere are a lot of cafés.
anynegative and questionsThere aren't any trains. / Are there any trains?
manymostly negative and questionsThere aren't many parks.

There is can be short: there's. There are is never short. With singular, use a/an (There is a bank).

watch.right: There is a park near here.
watch.why: In English, you need the word 'there'.
Agreement: tourists is plural, so we use are.
Use any in questions and negatives.
Use any in negatives, not some.

learn.title: The imperative
learn.html:
We use it to give directions, instructions, advice or orders. It has no subject (the subject is you, but we don't say it).

AffirmativeNegative
Base verb: Go straight. Turn left.Don't + base verb: Don't cross the street here. Don't worry.
  • With adjectives we use be: Be quiet. Don't be late.
  • We can join orders: Go straight, turn left and walk two blocks.
  • With please it sounds more polite: Turn left, please.

watch.why: After Don't, we use the verb without to.
The negative imperative is Don't, not No.
Always use Don't in the imperative.
No to. Use the base verb.

learn.title: Repeat directions to check them
learn.html:
After you get directions, repeat them in your own words and end with right? to check. If you made a mistake, the other person corrects you.

  • Excuse me, how do I get to the library? — ask for directions.
  • Turn left, then take the first street on the right. — give directions.
  • So, I turn left and take the first street on the left, right? — repeat to check.
  • No, the first street on the right. — correct.
  • Got it, thanks! — confirm and thank.

learn.title: Adjectives and reasons (because, this way)
learn.html:
We use it to describe a place and to give a reason for our recommendation.

  • The adjective goes before the noun and does not change in the plural: a beautiful city, beautiful buildings.
  • Nationalities start with a capital letter: Scottish, Mexican.
  • because (gives a reason): Take a map because the city is big. This way (in that way): Book early. This way, you have a good room.
  • Advice: Don't forget…, Remember…, Visit…, Try… Time: In August…, At night…
  • City names do not use the: Mexico City.

watch.right: because it is a big city
one of the most beautiful places
watch.why: Fixed structure: one of the most + adjective + plural noun.
City names do not use the.
The adjective does not change in the plural.

watch.wrong: because have a lot of places
watch.right: because it has a lot of places
watch.why: The subject is missing. With it, we use has.

learn.title: Useful expressions
learn.html:
• Is there a bank near here? — Yes, there is. It's next to the park. — ask if something is nearby.
  • Excuse me, how do I get to the library? — ask for directions.
  • Turn left, then take the first street on the right. — give directions.
  • So, I turn left and take the first street on the left, right? — repeat to check.
  • Got it, thanks! — confirm and thank.
  • Don't worry. — calm someone down.
  • Don't forget / Don't miss … — give advice.
  • … because … / This way, … — give reasons.
  • It's on the corner of … and … — say where a place is.

reading.title: A weekend in Guanajuato
reading.intro: Read Sofía's blog post and answer.
paragraphs: Hi everyone! I'm in Guanajuato this weekend, and it's a beautiful city. There are a lot of colorful houses and several old churches downtown. There's a big market near the main square, and there are some cafés next to the theater. The people are friendly, and there aren't many tourists on weekdays.
My hotel is on the corner of Alonso Street and Sopeña Street. It's small, but it's comfortable. There isn't any air conditioning, but it isn't a problem because the mornings are cool.

Here are my tips for visitors. Don't drive in the center, because the streets are very narrow. Walk, or take a bus. Go to the Alley of the Kiss in the afternoon, and don't forget your camera! Is there a good place for lunch? Yes, there is. Try the small restaurant across from the university. The enchiladas are awesome.
I love this city. It's a must for your next vacation!
